$description: BELLA part contracts: props, variants, a11y notes for each coded part. Not tokens (those come from Figma, tokens/figma/). Read by scripts/contract-parity.mjs, scripts/build-dsds.mjs, the test runner and the stories.

bella.name: Button
bella.rendersAs: a button, or one anchor with href
bella.description: Chip tertiary (22 Nov, her pick E): blue text only at rest (content/brand, 8.90:1 on the page ground), a pale blue wash and a blue underline on hover and focus; BELLA themes keep the ink tertiary. Buttons with real hierarchy: a flat primary plate on background/brand (ink in BELLA, near-white in BELLA dark; light blue #63b4e8 with a navy label in Chip), no gloss, no key edge, no shadow, never lifts; corner radius/lg (pill in BELLA, 8 in Chip), an outlined secondary, an ink text tier; one primary per view (brand refresh, 2026-09-22: no accent colour on buttons; the primary was flattened by the shared look, 8 Nov 2026). Labels are the theme's body face (DM Sans in BELLA, Lexend in Chip), 16 on a 22 line, weight 600, sentence case, never Unique.
usage: Hero CTA
Card 'Read more' action
Form submit
Contact send
Nav call to action (shape pill)
The primary contact CTA reads "Let's talk" (brand refresh, 2026-09-22)
dont: Do not render more than one primary per view: the flat primary plate is the single main action
Do not use for filters, toggles, or sort: that is FilterChip / SegmentedControl / Select territory
Do not set labels in Unique at any size
Do not build a neutral tier: it is retired
Do not lift a button on hover: lift is reserved for cards; hover is the label roll
Do not add the trace ring to a button: the trace is Card's affordance
bella.a11y: Measured 20 Nov 2026: primary label 13.90:1 on the plate in BELLA light and dark, 7.12:1 in Chip light and dark; on the hover plate 7.34:1 BELLA light, 9.54:1 BELLA dark, 7.54:1 Chip (AAA). Secondary label 16.13:1 light / 10.99:1 dark on the card. Control border 5.16:1 light on the card. Focus ring 4px with a 4px gap, outside: blue/600 #1865bb in the light themes (3.62:1 on the page), #63b4e8 in the dark themes (9.22:1). Focus-visible only. busy: aria-busy and aria-disabled while the job it started runs; clicks wait, focus stays; the turning icon is decorative and holds still under reduced motion.

anatomy.title: Shadow
anatomy.detail: none on the primary: no key edge, no drop, no highlight (shared look, 8 Nov 2026)

anatomy.title: Fill
anatomy.detail: flat plate, no gloss: ink in BELLA, near-white in BELLA dark, light blue #63b4e8 in Chip

anatomy.title: Box
anatomy.detail: 44px min, padding 0 / 20, radius/lg (pill in BELLA, 8 in Chip)

anatomy.title: Label
anatomy.detail: 16 on 22, weight 600, sentence case; DM Sans in BELLA, Lexend in Chip

anatomy.title: Focus ring
anatomy.detail: 4px, 4px gap, outside, focus-visible only

restState.description: One job per state. At rest the primary is a calm flat plate and a label: no gloss, no key edge, no shadow. Hover and focus-visible roll the label and shift the colour on every tier (primary plate, secondary fill, tertiary label); the button never lifts. Active is a small press down, primary only. Reduced motion: colour only, the shift stays and the roll and press drop. audit:quality asserts the invariants on every story rendering the component (root carries data-bella-component=button).

invariants.underlinedWhy: Figma Button 26:320 (read 19 Nov 2026): no tier carries an underline; tertiary is an ink label with a hover fill. The check now asserts zero underlines on every button, at rest and mid-roll.

bella.name: Card
bella.rendersAs: a div; with href one anchor, with onClick one button
bella.description: The one-card system: every card surface renders through this. Calm at rest, theme-aware by construction; the only fixed-light path is Peek, on purpose.
usage: Portfolio grid
Case-study cards
CHIP idea clusters
Dashboard tiles
dont: Do not nest cards inside cards
Do not use for navigation, that's nav-link's job
Do not nest links or buttons inside an interactive card: the card is ONE link or ONE button
Do not build a fixed-dark card, no fixed-dark path exists; peek (fixed always-light paper on navy) is the one recorded fixed-context exception
bella.a11y: Interactive cards render as a single anchor or button: one tab stop, no nested interactives. Name a card via ariaLabel when its visible content isn't the right name; media is aria-hidden when ariaLabel is set. Focus shows a visible ring (asserted in CI, both themes). Every card wears shadow.card at rest (peek stays flat); only interactive cards lift on hover and focus; prefers-reduced-motion keeps them still (the shadow still marks hover and focus). Card text sits on surface-card: text-muted 4.64:1 light / 6.03:1 dark, the worst pair (AA).

anatomy.title: Hover shadow
anatomy.detail: interactive cards only: 2px lift plus shadow; reduced motion keeps the shadow, drops the lift

anatomy.title: Rest shadow
anatomy.detail: every card but peek (re-scoped to none), Colour B, 2026-10-04

anatomy.title: Surface
anatomy.detail: the card fill

anatomy.title: Edge
anatomy.detail: 1px border-subtle hairline, radius 16 (--border-radius-card)

anatomy.title: Padding
anatomy.detail: 24px all round

anatomy.title: Focus ring
anatomy.detail: interactive cards only: 4px, 4px gap, outside, focus-visible only

bella.note: The variant token blocks elevated/glass/featured/inverse below predate the 0.3 Card and remain solely as value sources for the .bella-card-* utility classes emitted by build.py; they are NOT Card variants (the shipped API is default | peek; styling lives in Card.module.css). Their retirement rides on the glass-utility decision.

restState.description: The rest state is a contract (Colour B, Elleta, 2026-10-04; flat from 2026-09-19): only these layers may paint before hover/focus, and the shadow at rest is exactly shadow.card (peek re-scopes it to none and stays flat). audit:quality asserts the invariants on every story that renders the component (root carries data-bella-component=card).
hoverOnly: hover lift + shadow.hover, interactive cards only

invariants.note: resolved in the card's own context, so peek's re-scope to none counts
the inner panel stays inside the wrapper; the grid double-surface class of bug

bella.name: ResourceCard
bella.description: The folder card. A dark file window on top, a warm sheet below, and a tab folded up from the sheet itself so the two read as one piece of paper. Built for the toolkit gallery, where every item is a file you can open.
usage: The toolkit gallery, one card per installable skill
Any gallery where the items are files or documents with a type and a state
dont: Do not put a second link inside it: the whole card is one link, the Open action is a span that inherits it
Do not give the tab its own colour or a shadow: it is the sheet folded up, and a shadow breaks the fold
Do not write the description longer than two lines: it clamps, and a clamped third line reads as a bug
Do not colour the status dot yet: the ladder is unresolved (issue #1) and the neutral dot is the honest placeholder
bella.a11y: Verified 2026-07-30: title is text-primary on the surface, 12.81:1 light and 12.61:1 worst dark, AAA. Description is text-secondary, 7.74:1 light and 7.33:1 worst dark, AAA. Tab label and footer meta sit at the 16px reading floor, text-secondary, same ratios. The Open action is text-accent, 5.96:1 light and 5.30:1 worst dark, AA, and never stands on colour alone: it carries the word Open beside the arrow. One link per card, so one tab stop.

restState.description: At rest the card is the cover, the sheet, the tab and the notch, under Card's rest shadow (shadow.card, 2026-10-04); the lift and shadow.hover are hover and focus only, inherited from Card. The notch is painted from the same semantic surface token as the sheet, so it flips with the theme instead of biting a light hole in the navy card.

bella.name: Tag
bella.description: Non-interactive metadata. If you can click it, it is not a Tag.
usage: Card category labels
Project metadata rows
Mood and topic markers
dont: Do not make it clickable: narrowing a set is FilterChip's job
Do not add a border: the flat wash is what separates it from interactive chips
Do not set the label in an accent or status colour: tints are wash-only here
bella.a11y: Verified 2026-07-22: default label is text-secondary, 7.74:1 on the surface-inset wash in light and 7.33:1 worst in dark, AAA both. Accent label is text-accent on the accent-subtle wash, 5.25:1 worst in light and 5.30:1 worst in dark, AA. Non-interactive: no tab stop, no pointer affordance, cursor default.

restState.description: A Tag is entirely static: the wash and the label are the whole component, in every state. audit:quality asserts it never lifts or animates (root carries data-bella-component=tag).

bella.figma: style=solid (21 Nov 2026 publish): success, info, attention on the knockout fills, content/brand-knockout, no edge.

bella.name: StatusPill
bella.description: A status word in a pill. Non-interactive, one tint per state, readable in both themes.
usage: shape="dot": the state's mark only, the word kept as the accessible name (CHIP Today, Elleta 7 Nov 2026)
Current-focus marker
Project state rows
Availability notes
neutral: a state that is neither good nor bad (not tested, draft, disabled), no tint (CHIP, 2026-10-03)
Per variant, background, foreground and border are tokens, so a theme can restyle every state without touching the component (chip: soft washes, same-hue labels, no border; 7 Nov 2026)
dont: Do not make it clickable: a pill that toggles is a FilterChip
Do not colour the label with the state tint in BELLA's own themes. A theme may set a same-hue dark label only where it holds AAA on its wash, as chip does
Do not design new status UI on the carried tints without asking: the BELLA-native status ladder (issue #1) is pending and will restyle this
bella.a11y: Verified 2026-07-22: the label never depends on the tint. Accent label is text-accent, 5.66:1 light / 6.65:1 dark (AA). Success/info labels are text-secondary, AAA both themes. Tints as non-text rings: sage 4.33:1 on ground and 3.45:1 on navy (passes 3:1); steel 2.87:1 on ground (fails 3:1, wash-only per the recorded carry) and 5.20:1 on navy. The state is always readable from the word alone. CARRIED TINTS: pending the status-ladder sitting (issue #1).

restState.description: Entirely static, like Tag. audit:quality asserts it never lifts or animates (root carries data-bella-component=status-pill).

bella.name: FilterChip
bella.description: The toggle for narrowing a set. Pressed is a real state with real semantics, not a restyle.
usage: Work library skill/type filters
Any multi-select narrowing row
size compact: a long wrapping row of tag filters (CHIP Docs); the 44px target stays
dont: Do not use for mutually exclusive views: that is SegmentedControl
Do not make it a Button: a Button is reserved for true actions
Do not fake the state with colour alone: aria-pressed is the state, the fill is its paint
bella.a11y: Verified 2026-07-22: real button with aria-pressed, both themes. Default label text-secondary on transparent, 8.33:1 light / 9.20:1 dark (AAA). Pressed is the inverse fill: ground-on-ink 16.06:1 light, navy-on-dark-inverse equivalent in dark (AAA). Focus ring independent. Hit area 44px minimum (the touch-target token; the portfolio 32px chip is a recorded divergence, below the 2.5.5 Enhanced floor BELLA holds).

anatomy.detail: 44px min, padding 4 / 16, pill radius

anatomy.detail: border-subtle wash, the edge goes ink

restState.description: At rest the chip is the flat outline and its label; hover wash and the pressed fill are state paints. audit:quality asserts no elevation ever (root carries data-bella-component=filter-chip).

bella.name: SegmentedControl
bella.description: Pick one view among a few, all options visible. The selected state lives in ARIA, not just paint.
usage: Work library view switcher (Cards / Map / Table)
Any mutually exclusive view pick with few options
dont: Do not use for multi-select: that is FilterChip

Do not use radiogroup or tablist semantics: plain buttons with aria-current, per the recorded discovery pass (W3C APG radio rejected: single tab stop plus arrow-select blocks surveying; Primer SegmentedControl guidance matches)
Do not hide options behind it: if they do not all fit, it is a Select
bella.a11y: Verified 2026-07-22: each segment is a real button; Tab moves between segments, Enter/Space selects, arrows deliberately inert; aria-current=true marks the selection in the tree; the group carries a required aria-label. Segment icons are a decorative leading slot, aria-hidden, sized by the icon tokens; the text label always stays and carries the name (restored 2026-07-22 after the first extraction dropped it, a recorded divergence). Labels text-secondary 8.33:1 light / 9.20:1 dark (AAA); selected label text-accent on accent-subtle, 5.25:1 worst light / 5.30:1 worst dark (AA). Focus ring inset. Segments hit the 44px touch-target token (portfolio 38px is a recorded divergence).

restState.description: Flat always: the group border, dividers, and the selected fill are the whole paint. audit:quality asserts no elevation ever (root carries data-bella-component=segmented-control).

bella.name: Select
bella.description: For long lists only. If the options fit on screen, chips or a segmented control do it better.
usage: Sort order
Long single-choice lists
dont: Do not hand-roll a listbox: the native select owns the popup, the keyboard model, and the assistive-tech semantics
Do not drop the visible label: an unlabelled dropdown is a guess
Do not use it for a handful of visible options: SegmentedControl or FilterChip
bella.a11y: Verified 2026-07-22: native select labelled by containment; the platform popup needs no re-verification. Closed control: text-primary on surface, 16.92:1 light (AAA); label text-secondary 8.33:1 light / 9.20:1 dark (AAA). Option text at 14px is the closed-control field; the popup renders at platform size. Focus ring on the field; 44px min-height via the touch-target token.

restState.description: Flat always: field, border, chevron, label. audit:quality asserts no elevation ever (root carries data-bella-component=select).

bella.figma: Matches the published BellaComponents Select (149:163), 21 Nov 2026: text 16, 16 in, chevron 20, label gap 12, Button's focus ring. The open list is the platform's (native select), so its width, padding and option corners are not styled.

bella.name: Heading
bella.description: Newsreader 500 carries every heading tier, tight tracking, sentence case (shared look, 8 Nov 2026; was Figtree 600, heading weight, 2026-10-04, Elleta). Unique is retired (2026-10-08). Never inside a card.
usage: Page titles
Section heads
The hero headline
dont: Never inside a card: cards carry titles (DM Sans), not headings (contract-enforced by audit:quality)
Never below 32px for hero, page or section: only the subsection tier (24px) sits under the section ramp
bella.a11y: Verified 8 Nov 2026 (shared look): text-primary 15.04:1 light / 16.26:1 dark on the page, AAA. The accent segment is the muted half-line, text-secondary, 7.95:1 light / 9.41:1 dark (AAA). Semantic level decouples from the visual tier via the as prop, so the outline stays honest.

restState.description: Type only, entirely static; and a Heading may never sit inside a Card. audit:quality asserts both (root carries data-bella-component=heading).

invariants.note: Headings never render inside a card

bella.name: Icon
bella.description: The only way BELLA renders an icon. Iconoir glyphs from an inlined registry, icon-token sized, always currentColor; decorative by default, a label makes it meaningful. Also carries the official one-colour tool marks (Storybook, Figma, GitHub, Notion), filled in the context ink beside a link's label.
usage: Segment glyphs
The Select chevron
Any leading icon slot
dont: Do not put id attributes inside an icon SVG: the glyph renders more than once (the Button label roll duplicates it), so an id-referenced gradient or clip would collide; draw with paths and currentColor only (audit:quality enforces)

Do not mix icon sets or draw one-off SVGs: Iconoir is the ONLY source (declared 2026-07-22) and every glyph lives in the registry, nothing inline (audit:quality enforces); the one exception is the four tool marks (Storybook, Figma, GitHub, Notion), the official one-colour shapes from Simple Icons (CC0), filled not stroked, shapes unchanged
Do not import an icon library component surface: the registry carries the paths BELLA ships (borrow-behavior-only, recorded)
Do not hardcode an icon colour: currentColor inherits the themed ink
Do not let a meaningful icon stand without text unless its accessible name is proven in a Behavior story; decorative is the default and needs no name
bella.a11y: Verified 2026-07-22: aria-hidden by default (decorative); with label, role=img plus aria-label. Colour is always currentColor, so contrast rides on the text token of the context. Sizes from the icon tokens (sm 16 / md 20 / lg 24), stroke from icon.stroke.

restState.description: Static glyph. audit:quality has no elevation to assert; the invariants hold trivially.

bella.name: Avatar
bella.description: A person or entity as a circle. An image when there is one, the initials of the name when there is not, never an empty grey disc.
usage: A portrait beside a name and role
An author or testimonial attribution
The identity slot in a contact panel
dont: Do not use it as a decorative circle: an Avatar stands for someone, a plain disc is artwork
Do not ship it without a name: the initials fallback is the point, an empty disc is a bug
Do not put a status dot on it yet: the status ladder is unresolved (issue #1)
bella.a11y: Verified 2026-07-30: initials are text-secondary on the surface-inset wash, 7.74:1 in light and 7.33:1 worst in dark, AAA both. With an image the img carries alt; without one the root is role=img labelled by name and the initials are aria-hidden, so it announces once, as the person, never as two letters.

restState.description: An Avatar is entirely static. The ring is a rest-state affordance, not a hover one: it is either on or off, it never animates. audit:quality asserts it never transforms or animates (root carries data-bella-component=avatar).

bella.name: Eyebrow
bella.description: Sans label above a heading, 14px, no tracking, no caps (label style; mono is for tokens, code and hashes only, Elleta, 2026-10-03). Signals context or category.
usage: Above hero headlines
Above section titles
Above card groupings
dont: Do not use as a heading: eyebrows complement a heading, never replace one
Never an accent colour: wayfinding is not action
Never below 16px, never tracked, never uppercased
bella.a11y: 16px floor. muted: text-secondary, 7.09:1 worst light / 7.06:1 worst dark (AAA). ink: text-primary (AAA). Verified 2026-09-22.

restState.description: Type only, entirely static.

bella.name: Input
bella.description: Labelled, stateful, honest about errors. The form is the channel, so the fields carry the trust. 23 Nov (code only): type=password is masked with a Show / Hide button at the end of the field, autocomplete, spellcheck and capitals off, and the value lives only in the field itself, never in text, a label or another attribute.
usage: Contact form fields
Any labelled free-text entry; multiline renders the textarea
dont: Do not use placeholder as the label: the label is always rendered and wired with for/id
Do not fake errors with colour alone: aria-invalid plus a role=alert message wired via aria-describedby is the pattern
Do not signal an error with colour alone: the danger border always comes with the WarningCircle icon, the message and aria-invalid
bella.a11y: Verified 2026-07-22: real label element (for/id), 8.33:1 light / 9.20:1 dark (AAA). Field text text-primary on surface, 16.92:1 light (AAA); placeholder text-muted, 4.67:1 worst (AA, opacity reset for Firefox). Suggestion (Input 1608:3716): the ghost question is the placeholder in content/subtle (8.53:1 Chip light, 10.99:1 Chip dark on the surface, AAA); the ↵ keycap is aria-hidden and the field is described by "Press Enter to ask"; Enter sends it, typing replaces it. Errors (status tokens, 2026-09-22): aria-invalid + role=alert message via aria-describedby; 2px danger-border (3:1+ on every surface), WarningCircle icon, message in danger-text (5.84:1 light on panel, 6.86:1 dark on raised; AA). Focus: the 4px focus ring (4px gap, outside) plus an ink edge; an invalid field keeps its danger edge under the ring. 44px min-height.

Footer links

Do not rely on color alone, always underlined or weight-shifted on hover

Footer navigation

bella.name: Section

usage: Every block of a page below the PageHeader
Case-study sections

bella.name: Modal

usage: Dialogs
Sheets
Confirmations

The footer sign-off (size full-bleed)
The BELLA name on its own pages
dont: Never below 32px tall
Never recolour the pattern: it only comes from color.pattern.*
Never as body type or a heading: it is a mark, not a typeface
Never animate it

Never in colour: the colour pattern belongs to the wordmark
Never interactive

bella.name: Callout

Static: no interaction, no motion.

gap: a visible placeholder for content still to be written
dont: Not a status banner: no info, success, warning or error variants
Never interactive: no hover, no lift, never a link as a whole
No colour: hairline or dashed muted frame only, no chip fill, no accent

bella.name: Tabs
bella.description: Switch between panels that share one place on the page (CHIP components, 2026-10-03). W3C APG tabs with automatic activation; each tab owns a panel. Optional run state per tab, drawn as a dot and spoken as text.
usage: CHIP workspace switcher
CHIP terminal switcher (with run state)
Any set of panels where one shows at a time
dont: Do not use to switch a view of the same content: that is SegmentedControl
Do not use for navigation between pages: that is NavList
Do not mark the selected tab with colour alone: ink text plus the 2px ink bar
Do not render panels without tabPanelProps: aria-controls must resolve

Labels text-secondary 7.94:1 light / 9.06:1 dark at rest (AAA), selected text-primary 18.73:1 / 16.60:1 on the page (AAA); the selected bar is ink (non-text, far above 3:1). Run state is a filled ink dot or an idle border-strong ring (3.00:1 worst) and also text in the name. Focus ring 4px, inset. Tabs hit the 44px touch-target token.

bella.name: VariantTile
bella.description: A variant thumbnail: a mini preview with its label under. Selected draws a 2px brand edge; the check badge marks a copied or done state.
usage: The states strip under the stage on CHIP Components
Picking a variant from thumbnails
dont: Do not put live controls in the preview: it is a picture (inert)
Do not use it for navigation: it picks a state in place
bella.a11y: With onClick the tile is one button named by its label, aria-pressed for selected, BELLA's focus ring. The preview is inert and hidden from the accessibility tree. The check badge is an image named Done. Labels are content-subtle (7:1) or content-default on surface and default-hover.

bella.name: ProgressTarget
bella.description: The target drawn into a meter (Figma Progress target 1168:72541, 22 Nov 2026, decided: a dashed marker and label): a 1.5 dashed line in border/brand at target %, from its label to 4 below the 8 bar, and a "Target n%" Tag (outline, number face 600) in the 32 row above the bar. Up to 50 the label starts at the line; above 50 it ends at it. Also exports TargetMark, the private 4-wide mark the Check row legend still uses. showLabel off draws the dash alone (23 Nov).
usage: Progress bar with a target (Stat card, Check row)
Check list header legend (TargetMark)
dont: Never a second target colour: blue (border/brand) only
No overhang past the bar (21 Nov publish)
bella.a11y: The marker and its label sit in the bar's aria-hidden track, so they are not read twice; the target is spoken in the bar's value text ("80%, target 90%", as Stat card sets it). Label ink 7:1 on its Tag; the dash 3:1 on the card.
bella.figma: Matches the published BellaComponents Progress target (1168:72541) and _Target mark, 21 Nov 2026: 8 tall, 1px outside edge color/background/surface. Height is size/8 (published in Foundations 22 Nov).

bella.name: Marker
bella.description: The keyword mark (Figma BellaComponents Marker 1600:45992, 22 Nov 2026): the key word or phrase in a line at weight 600 over a soft blue underline (color/background/wash/blue-strong), the lower 10 of the 24 line, 2 above its bottom. Inline, so it wraps with its line. Bold is for keywords only, and every keyword gets this underline.
usage: The one key phrase in an Ask BELLA answer's verdict line
The words to take away in a doc paragraph or a Why line
A keyword inside a Step or record title
dont: Do not mark a link: that is Link
Do not mark a status: that is Tag
Do not mark a whole sentence, or more than one phrase per paragraph
bella.a11y: A <mark> element, so screen readers can announce a highlight. The phrase keeps the ink of its line on the page colour and on the band, 7:1 or more in all four themes; the band is decoration under it. Forced colours: Mark and MarkText.

bella.name: BarChart
bella.description: Runs over time as rounded bars, one bar per time slot, from a visible zero baseline: passes in green and failures in red on top with a cross mark, so a failure is found at a glance and never by colour alone (Gate runs, "C · Apple style"). A range (D, W, M, Y), the number with its unit and one meta line above, thin dashed gridlines, the latest bar labelled. Hover, touch or arrow keys pick a bar: a 1px guide, an outline on that bar (the others stay as they are) and a callout above the plot. A table of the same data and a one-line summary sit behind every chart. Bars grow from the base and morph between ranges; reduced motion shows the end state at once. 23 Nov (code only): the number row wraps at 320; axisUnit prints what the axis counts once above the plot; an empty slot prints no number; calloutText words the callout from the data; onSlotSelect makes slots with failures buttons (click, Enter, Space) that open what failed.
usage: Gate runs on CHIP Health and the Work board (22 Nov 2026)
dont: Not a trend over a long time with many points (a line chart)
Not a part of a whole (never a pie or donut)
Never red and green alone: the cross mark and the legend words carry the failure
Never gaps joined by a line across them
bella.a11y: A group named by its title, described by the summary line (always present). Each slot is a focusable image with roving tabindex, named "14:15-14:30, 3 runs, 3 failed, contracts"; arrow keys, Home and End move between slots and the callout follows, Esc closes it. The callout is decoration: the slot's name says the same. Pass and fail differ by position, the cross mark and the legend words, never colour alone. A Show table button swaps the chart for a DataTable of the same data. Bars 3:1 on the card in all four themes, text 7:1, numbers tabular. Reduced motion: bars stand at full height at once.
bella.figma: Matches BellaComponents BarChart 1737:304 (22 Nov 2026): state default and scrub, view chart and table; Range is SegmentedControl with Show segment 4 (stretch). Differences kept on purpose: the table view carries DataTable's visible caption, and a Show table button sits at the right of the legend row (the Figma table view has neither).

bella.name: FloatingPanel
bella.description: A panel detached from its drawer into a small window that floats over any page, so you can watch an agent (the Terminal) and keep working. A title bar with a grip, the title, an optional status (a StatusDot, no wash) and a Stop button, Dock and Close; a body slot holding the drawer's content as it is. Moved by dragging the title bar or the arrow keys on the focused bar, kept fully on screen. Esc or Dock puts it back; Close closes it.
usage: The Terminal detached from its Drawer on every CHIP page (22 Nov 2026)
dont: Not a dialog that needs an answer (a modal)
Not a hover hint (Tooltip)
No resize corner: the window has one size
bella.a11y: role=dialog, aria-modal=false, named by its title; the page behind stays usable. The title bar is focusable (tabindex 0) with the description "Arrow keys move it, Esc docks it"; arrows move it 8 a press, Shift 40, and it stops 16 from the window edge. Focus moves to the title bar when it opens and back to the button that opened it when it docks or closes. Dock and Close have names ("Dock Terminal", "Close Terminal") and Tooltips; every control is a 44 target with the focus ring. Reduced motion: it appears and goes at once.
bella.figma: Matches BellaComponents FloatingPanel 1739:20 (22 Nov 2026): Title, Show status, Show action, Body slot. Arrow step 8 and Shift 40 as the published description says. The Dock button uses SidebarExpand until the Icon set gains a dock icon (Figma gap noted in the spec).

bella.name: ToolColumn
bella.description: The thin column of view tools beside a stage: zoom in, fit, zoom out, then light or dark, mark up and compare. Icon-only tertiary buttons, each named by a Tooltip on its right; a zoom readout ("200%") 16 right of and 8 under the column. Zoom steps 25, 50, 75, 100, 150, 200, 300, 400; light or dark, mark up and compare are toggles. It replaces a control bar so the part gets the stage.
usage: Components workbench and Playground stage, top left inside it (22 Nov 2026)
dont: Not page actions (PageHeader)
Not a row of choices (SegmentedControl)
bella.a11y: role=toolbar, aria-orientation=vertical, named "View tools". One tab stop (roving tabindex): Up, Down, Home and End move between the tools; + and - zoom one step, Shift+1 fits. Each tool is a 44 target named by its aria-label (the same words as its Tooltip, shown on hover and on keyboard focus); the three toggles carry aria-pressed. The readout is a status. Focus ring on every tool.
bella.figma: Matches BellaComponents ToolColumn (22 Nov 2026): View group, Divider, Tools group, Show zoom. Icons ZoomIn, ZoomOut and Expand were added to the Icon registry from the Figma Icon set; Compare uses Copy until the set gains a two-pane glyph. The Tooltip shows at once on hover (the Figma 500 ms hover delay is not in the Tooltip part yet).

bella.name: Branch
bella.description: One branch of a mind map: an S-curve between any two points that leaves and arrives level, in one of five brand colours (pink, navy, ochre, stone, blue) by name. regular is 3 wide (root to stage), thin 2 (stage to step), round ends. Motion as MapLine: draw (map 900ms, pick 250ms, start to end), travel (one soft pass, then rests), nothing moves under reduced motion. Decorative.
usage: Processes mind maps (23 Nov 2026)
dont: Not a straight or right-angle line between rows (MapLine)
Not a leader to a part (Leader)
bella.a11y: Decorative: aria-hidden; the words beside it carry the meaning. The colour names the stage only; a step's state is always a shape and a word. Marks 3:1 on the work area. Reduced motion: fully drawn, no draw-in, no highlight.
bella.figma: Code only, 23 Nov 2026 (her pick A, Processes as mind maps); Figma catch-up after Tue 24 Nov.

bella.name: MapLeaf
bella.description: One step of a mind map as bare text on a branch end: name, then a state shape and word, then an optional measured line in plain text. A button, 44 tall, with MapNode's selected state (light-blue fill, 2px brand edge), a 1px edge for a linked step and MapNode's focus ring.
usage: Processes mind maps and, in a BranchGroup, on a phone (23 Nov 2026)
dont: Not a boxed step (MapNode)
Not a status on its own (StatusDot)
bella.a11y: A button with aria-pressed. State is a shape (ticked circle, triangle, diamond, minus square, dashed circle) plus its word, never colour alone; the shape is decorative. Text 7:1; target 44 tall; focus ring 4 wide, 4 gap.
bella.figma: Code only, 23 Nov 2026 (her pick A, Processes as mind maps); Figma catch-up after Tue 24 Nov.

bella.name: MapLabel
bella.description: A node of a mind map that is not a step. root: the map's name in a rounded 20 box with a 1px strong edge, 64 tall, centred. stage: a stage's name as bare bold text (Lexend 600, 20), up to 148 wide, where its branches meet. Not interactive.
usage: Processes mind maps (23 Nov 2026)
dont: Not a step (MapLeaf, MapNode)
Not a section title (SectionHead) or page heading (PageHeader)
bella.a11y: Plain text; pass `as` to make it a heading when it titles a region. Text 7:1.
bella.figma: Code only, 23 Nov 2026 (her pick A, Processes as mind maps); Figma catch-up after Tue 24 Nov.

bella.name: BranchGroup
bella.description: A stage on a phone mind map: a white row with a 4 wide colour bar at the left, the stage's name, its count and a plus or minus. The head is a 48 tall button with aria-expanded; open, it shows its steps (MapLeaf) below. One open at a time is the caller's rule.
usage: Processes mind maps on a phone (23 Nov 2026)
dont: Not a disclosure of long text (Disclosure)
Not a group name in a wide layout (GroupHead)
bella.a11y: A button with aria-expanded and aria-controls naming the list; the plus or minus is decorative. The colour bar names the stage only. 48 tall target; focus ring 4 wide, drawn inside.
bella.figma: Code only, 23 Nov 2026 (her pick A, Processes as mind maps); Figma catch-up after Tue 24 Nov.

bella.name: LineChart
bella.description: A trend over time: a 1.5 round-capped line over a soft gradient of its tone (fading to nothing at the baseline) on dashed thin gridlines. Hover, touch drag or the arrow keys (Home, End, Escape) stand a 14 wide fully rounded scrubber on the line; above it a dark pill says the change against the previous point or a reference, the value and the label, and the same words go to a live region. Scale starts at zero; baseline=auto needs a stated reason, printed under the chart. Tones success, warning, danger, info, neutral, brand. draw map 900ms or pick 250ms (line left to right, area fades in, scrubber settles). variant=compact is a sparkline with a dot on the last point. Always a one-line summary and a visually hidden table; showViewToggle shows the table on request. Reduced motion draws the end state.
usage: Trends on Health, the audit score, Gate runs as an alternative view, History activity, and the Drift drawer headline as a compact sparkline (23 Nov 2026)
dont: Not runs with passes and failures per slot (BarChart)
Not a single figure with a tiny trend line (Stat)
Not for comparing categories (bars); never a pie
bella.a11y: The plot is a slider (arrow keys, Home, End, Escape) with aria-valuetext in words; the callout's words are in a polite live region; a visually hidden table holds the same data and a one-line summary is always present. Direction is a triangle and a word, never colour alone. Line 3:1 on the ground, pill 7:1. Reduced motion: drawn at once, nothing slides.
bella.figma: Code only, 23 Nov 2026 (her reference picture, layout only); Figma catch-up after Tue 24 Nov.

bella.name: MapNode
bella.description: One step of a process map on CHIP Processes: its name and its health, a flat 176-wide box (no shadow) with a strong edge. Tone default, attention (the warning edge: a step that needs you) or blocked (a neutral dot, "Blocked: <what>"); selected is the light-blue fill with the 2px brand edge. The dot meets the title's left edge and the status word starts 8 after it. Joined by MapLine direction=curve.
usage: Processes maps and the System map (22 Nov 2026)
dont: Not a grid item (Card)
Not a status on its own (StatusDot)
Not a step in a short sequence (Step)
bella.a11y: A button with aria-pressed. The dot is a StatusDot named by the status word, so the word is read once; the visible word is aria-hidden. Text 7:1; the resting edge is a hairline (decoration), the selected edge 4.05:1; the status is never colour alone (the word says it). Focus ring 4 wide, 4 gap, corner 16.
bella.figma: Matches BellaComponents MapNode 794:169078 (22 Nov 2026): tone default, attention, blocked; selected; 176 wide, corner 12, flat. Show hotspot (the Pin badge on the corner) is not built: the map board places its pins itself.

bella.name: Slide
bella.description: One 16:9 slide drawn at 1280 by 720 and scaled to the width it is given; a card frame that holds BELLA parts.
usage: A deck stage, the all-slides grid and slide thumbnails (deck plan, 23 Nov 2026)
dont: Not a page (PageHeader and Section)
Not a card in a grid (Card)
bella.a11y: role group named "slide" with the label as its name. Content is drawn at the 16 px floor and scaled down only to fit; a slide is never scaled up past its design size.
bella.figma: Code first from the deck plan (23 Nov 2026); the Figma part follows after Tue 24 Nov.

bella.name: TitleSlide
bella.description: The opening or closing slide: an eyebrow, the hero title, one lead sentence and a foot line, centred on a Slide.
usage: First and last slide of a deck (deck plan, 23 Nov 2026)
dont: Not a content slide (Slide)
Not a page heading (PageHeader)
bella.a11y: The title is an h2 inside the slide group; the group is named by label or the title text.
bella.figma: Code first from the deck plan (23 Nov 2026); the Figma part follows after Tue 24 Nov.

bella.name: DeckBar
bella.description: The controls under a presented deck: Back, the count with one segment per slide, Next, and Notes and All slides.
usage: Under the deck stage in the Present page (deck plan, 23 Nov 2026)
dont: Not a tour step (TourStep)
Not site navigation (SectionNav)
bella.a11y: A labelled group. Back and Next are disabled, not hidden, at the ends. Notes is a toggle (aria-pressed). The count is read in the progress name; the visible text is hidden from the tree to avoid a double read.
bella.figma: Code first from the deck plan (23 Nov 2026); the Figma part follows after Tue 24 Nov.

bella.name: VideoPlayer
bella.description: A silent 16:9 clip with a still, captions and a visible Play or Pause button; autoplays muted unless the person wants less motion.
usage: The opening film of a deck (deck plan, 23 Nov 2026)
dont: Not for sound or long video: no volume or scrub
Not a hero background loop
bella.a11y: The video is named by label; captions are on by default. Autoplay is skipped under prefers-reduced-motion and the poster stays until Play is pressed. The button is a BELLA Button with its 44 target; it does not rely on the native control bar.
bella.figma: Code first from the deck plan (23 Nov 2026); the Figma part follows after Tue 24 Nov.

bella.name: RunIndicator
bella.description: One persistent pill that says whether anything is running, which run, its step and how long it has been going; idle, running, done and failed are all drawn so a quiet screen is never ambiguous.
usage: CHIP header, beside Search (23 Nov 2026, feedback and sense of time)
dont: Not a progress bar (Progress)
Not a toast (Toast): it stays
No second spinner on the page
bella.a11y: Button when it opens the list (aria-expanded), otherwise role=img; always named by the whole sentence ("Running: Fix CheckRow, Step 3 of 7, 2:41 so far"). A status region announces start and end, never the ticking time. 44 high; edge 3:1; narrow screens keep the ring and the count and the name stays full.
bella.figma: Not drawn in Figma yet: built in code first on 23 Nov 2026 for the demo; Figma follows (named gap).

bella.name: TimelineRow
bella.description: One job in the Activity timeline: a rounded row with its state ring (running, done, queued, did not land), the title and one line of when, how long and how far.
usage: CHIP Activity list in the drawer (23 Nov 2026)
dont: Not a Card (a message or a result is a Notification)
Never colour alone: the state is a ring shape and a word
bella.a11y: A button when it opens the run, a plain row otherwise; the state is read as a word (Running, Done, Queued, Did not land). 44 or more high; focus ring on keyboard focus.
bella.figma: Not drawn in Figma yet: built in code first on 23 Nov 2026 for the demo; Figma follows (named gap).

bella.name: LastRun
bella.description: The stamp under any action that can be run again: what, when, how long, what it found, as one line ("Ran 09:24 · 2 s · nothing new").
usage: CHIP Check again, Refresh and Test (23 Nov 2026)
dont: Not a Tag
Not for a time on its own (Stat)
bella.a11y: Plain text in a paragraph; a failed run begins with the words "Did not land", so colour is never the only signal. 16px, 1.5 line height; subtle ink 7:1 or more on the page.
bella.figma: Not drawn in Figma yet: built in code first on 23 Nov 2026 for the demo; Figma follows (named gap).

bella.name: Sparkline
bella.description: A mini trend line (23 Nov 2026; moved out of Stat, rule 2: a mark used in two parts is its own part): a 1px ink line and an end dot in a 80 by 24 drawing, a scrubber with BELLA's Tooltip as the callout, a one-line summary and a table behind it. It zooms to the series' own low and high, so a small change still reads as a slope; the numbers are in the summary, the table and the callout. Stat and StatCard draw it.
usage: Stat (series)
Stat card (series, under the number)
dont: Never invent a series: it is the values that were kept
Never read the height as an amount: it is a shape
bella.a11y: role=img with a name and a description (the one-line summary); the keyboard scrubber (arrow keys, Home, End, Esc) says each point in a polite live region; the table of points is visually hidden. The hit area is 44 tall. Reduced motion: the end state at once.
bella.figma: Drawn inside the published Stat (22 Nov); no Figma part of its own yet.
